title: Workload-aware quantization gating + drift-aware thresholding for int8/int4 (AWQ & GPTQ)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a repeatable pipeline and gating rules to decide when a quantization profile (AWQ or GPTQ, int8 or int4) is safe to promote for a given workload. Unlike prior work that reports single global thresholds, this ticket scopes a per-workload, drift-aware thresholding approach with conservative rollout gates to prevent quality regressions in production. We will evaluate both static profile calibration and live drift triggers that tighten thresholds when input distribution shifts. Target workloads: conversational chat, abstractive summarization, search reranking, and code generation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pipeline can run batched evals comparing FP16 baseline vs AWQ/GPTQ int8/int4 variants for each workload automatically. 2) Derived composite quality metric (see 'metric_definition') and per-workload thresholds are computed and stored in the console. 3) A gating rule (promote / block / canary) based on thresholds + drift detector is implemented. 4) Dashboard shows per-model, per-profile migration risk with recommended action and a linked PR for rollout. 5) A documented rollback policy and synthetic test to catch clear regressions is added to the runtime rollout flow.
metric_definition: CompositeQuality = weighted_sum({semantic_sim: 0.45, factuality_score: 0.25, token_perplexity_delta: 0.15, behavioral_tests_pass_rate: 0.15}). Semantic_sim uses BERTScore on outputs vs FP16; factuality_score is a fact-precision probe (QA-based) aggregated by passage; perplexity_delta penalizes increased perplexity; behavioral_tests are a small curated prompt suite (safety + correctness). The composite is normalized so FP16 baseline = 100. Thresholds are expressed as allowable percent drop (e.g., -1.5% for chat, -0.8% for rerank).
tasks: Define per-workload acceptance thresholds and mapping to rollout actions (block/canary/promote)
Implement batched eval runner to test FP16 vs AWQ/GPTQ (int8/int4) across curated datasets
Add drift detector based on embedding distribution KL + feature histograms
Integrate composite metric computation and store results in console metrics API
Create dashboard widget showing risk score and recommended action for each model/profile
Write rollout gating logic and unit/e2e tests to enforce rollback on regression
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete: ran small sweep for two models (openlm-7b variant, redwood-7b) comparing AWQ int8 vs GPTQ int8 on chat workload — AWQ had slightly higher token perplexity but matched BERTScore on average. 2026-03-06: Decided to move from single-metric BLEU-like gating to CompositeQuality to better capture semantic and factual regressions. 2026-03-10: Implemented batched eval runner prototype and validated data plumbing for conversational and summarization datasets. 2026-03-13: Found edge case where code generation tasks show large variance in BERTScore; adding behavioral tests to better surface label-free correctness. Currently wiring dashboard and gating hooks.
results_summary: Preliminary runs (n=500 prompts per workload): AWQ int8 vs FP16: CompositeQuality delta mean = -0.9% (chat), -0.6% (summarization), -0.4% (rerank), -3.2% (codegen). GPTQ int8 vs FP16: delta mean = -0.7% (chat), -0.5% (summarization), -0.3% (rerank), -2.8% (codegen). Int4 variants show larger deltas and higher variance; safe promotion candidates at int4 are few and workload-specific. Drift simulation (synthetic domain shift) tightened safe thresholds by ~0.6% on average, supporting need for dynamic gates.
review_feedback: PM: Prefer conservative thresholds for customer-facing models; mark codegen as 'manual review only' until behavioral tests mature.
Security: No KMS change; verify that eval payloads are scrubbed for PII when using customer datasets.
SRE: Ensure the eval runner can be rate-limited and does not contend with production capacity; prefer off-peak scheduling.

notes:
- We intentionally weight semantic similarity highest because customer complaints tend to correlate with degraded semantics rather than raw token loss.
- Codegen requires a separate 'functional correctness' harness (fuzz + unit execution) before any automated promotion.
- Consider publishing a 'safe profile' tag in model catalog when a profile passes gated checks; this will be useful for Dedicated/Private customers to opt in.
- If drift detector signals sustained shift, the gate should escalate to manual review rather than automatic rollback to avoid flapping.
